title: Regional capacity smoothing and procurement triggers
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet defines a lightweight smoothing model for regional GPU capacity forecasts, recommended reorder triggers per SKU/region, and an action matrix for shortfall events. Goal: avoid emergency air-freight orders by making earlier, smaller replenishment decisions while keeping reserve costs reasonable.

High-level approach (summary):
- Compute a smoothed consumption signal per region + SKU using exponential moving average (EMA) of 14d and 60d windows. Use the 14d for near-term burst detection, 60d for baseline trend.
- Translate smoothed consumption to a rolling 12-week demand projection with conservative growth factor (1.05x multiplier for regions with >10% QoQ growth).
- Maintain a rolling safety buffer measured in standardized-days-of-capacity (SDC): target SDC by region = 21 days for NA, 28 days for EU, 35 days for APAC (longer lead times).
- Reorder when (Projected burn in lead_time + target_SDC) - OnHand <= reorder_threshold. Thresholds differ by SKU criticality.

Key parameters (current recommended defaults):
- EMA alpha (14d): 0.18
- EMA alpha (60d): 0.033
- Growth multiplier: region_growth_adj = max(1.0, 1.05 if QoQ_growth_rate > 10%)
- Lead time assumptions (procurement to rack-ready):
  - NA: standard GPU SKUs: 6-8 weeks; special orders (custom cooling): 10-14 weeks
  - EU: standard: 8-10 weeks; special: 12-16 weeks
  - APAC: standard: 10-16 weeks; shipping+customs spike: up to 22 weeks
- Target SDC: NA=21, EU=28, APAC=35
- Reorder_thresholds by SKU class:
  - Class A (high-performance, e.g., H100-like): reorder when projected shortfall > 0.9 * daily_peak * 14 (i.e., two-week peak coverage)
  - Class B (general purpose, e.g., A10/A100-like): reorder when projected shortfall > 0.6 * daily_peak * 21
  - Class C (inference-optimized low-end): reorder when projected shortfall > 0.4 * daily_peak * 28

Regional SKU mix guidance (examples):
- NA: heavier on Class A and B (target fleet mix: 40% A / 45% B / 15% C). Prioritize Class A in us-west for hosted low-latency zones.
- EU: balanced: 30% A / 50% B / 20% C. Hold additional B-capacity in west-eu staging to smooth arrivals.
- APAC: lean on B/C: 20% A / 50% B / 30% C due to longer lead times and cost sensitivity.

Procurement cadence and staggered arrivals:
- Avoid single big orders for a SKU across global regions. Instead: tranche orders by region and split into 3 arrival waves spaced by 3–4 weeks to mitigate single-shipment risk.
- For Class A, prefer 2 tranches if lead time > 10 weeks; for Class B/C, 3 tranches.
- Maintain an active rolling 16-week order pipeline: each week review the 0–16 week slice for gap detection.

Shortfall action matrix (operational playbook):
- Green (projected shortfall < 5% of regional pool): auto-apply short-term routing rules (burst to other regions for non-data-residency-sensitive workloads), no procurement action.
- Yellow (5–15% shortfall): trigger Capacity Ops to increase staggered-orders by 1 tranche and open vendor expedite options. Alert SRE on routing changes.
- Red (>15% or >2 consecutive weeks of rising EMA): raise incident to infra leadership, evaluate emergency market buys (air freight) and reduce non-critical background batch workloads by configurable % (recommended initial target 30%).

Example calculation (NA / Class A):
- OnHand GPUs: 300 units
- EMA14 burn (units/day): 12
- Projected 8-week burn = EMA14 * 56 = 672 units (adjust with growth multiplier)
- Lead time (NA Class A): 8 weeks (56 days) -> projected incoming window must cover 672 units + target_SDC (21 days * EMA14 = 252 units) = 924 units needed over 8 weeks
- Shortfall = 924 - 300 = 624 -> triggers immediate procurement tranche scheduling (Yellow/Red depending on sustained trend).

Data sources and owners:
- OnHand and allocations: Inventory DB (owner: Aisha Patel)
- Burn/usage signal: routing_metrics ingestion (owner: Maya Chen)
- Purchase order status: Procurement tracker (owner: Liam O'Connor)
- Vendor lead time estimates: Procurement ops (owner: Priya Desai)

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- How to encode air-freight cost into reorder decision algorithm? current plan: flag emergency buys separately; do not let cost trade off cause understock of Class A.
- APAC customs volatility not well modeled; need to add a customs_delay factor based on historical variance per port.
- Should we keep a small pooled global Class A buffer that can be moved in crises? legal/data controls make movement non-trivial; needs legal sign-off.

Operational TODOs (near-term):
- [ ] Build an automated weekly report that computes SDC and shortfall per region (owner: Maya).
- [ ] Add customs_delay parameter to lead time table with historical variance (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Draft quick-runbook for Yellow incidents to be consumed by Capacity Ops (owner: Liam).
- [ ] Sync with Procurement on vendor tranche minimums and expedite premiums (owner: Aisha).

Appendix: quick heuristics for planners:
- If user-facing latency SLOs are at risk, prioritize Class A redeploys over batch capacity.
- When splitting tranches, avoid >40% of region demand in a single tranche.
- Treat vendor holdbacks (allocation caps) as regularized constraints in the projection model instead of ad-hoc exceptions.

Notes: rough-sheet, will convert to Confluence playbook after sign-off from Procurement and Legal. Contains working assumptions — expect parameter updates after next vendor RFQ cycle.
